cards.text: Jesus has just finished teaching up on the mountain (Matthew 5:1-7:29). Now He comes down, and large crowds follow Him. Friend, the biggest crowd I ever had was a twist tie and two dead batteries in the back of a junk drawer.
Then, suddenly, a man with leprosy comes and kneels before Jesus. No appointment, no heads-up, no “you free Tuesday?” Just SUDDENLY.

cards.question: The man with leprosy kneels before Jesus and calls Him Lord. What does he say Jesus can do for him?
The leper tells Jesus He can make him clean if He is willing.
Jesus answers the leper with more than words. What does He do?

answers.text: He reaches out and touches him
He tells him to wash in the Jordan
He puts mud on his skin

cards.question: The leper asked if Jesus was willing. Jesus answers him: “I am ___,” He said. “Be clean!”
Jesus says “Be clean!” and the leper's healing takes a few days to finish.

cards.text: Friend, I waited YEARS for somebody to open my drawer, and this man waits zero seconds. Then Jesus instructs him, “See that you don’t tell anyone.”

cards.question: Jesus tells the man He healed of leprosy not to tell anyone. Who does Jesus send him to show himself to?

cards.text: He's also to offer the gift Moses prescribed, as a testimony to them. Then Jesus enters Capernaum, and a centurion, an army officer, comes and pleads with Him.

cards.question: The centurion in Capernaum pleads with Jesus. Who is he asking for help for?

cards.text: He says, “Lord, my servant lies at home, paralyzed and in terrible agony.” I bet this one has been keeping him up at night.

cards.question: When the centurion tells Him about his servant, Jesus says He will go and heal him.

cards.text: Jesus is ready to head over. Then the centurion answers, and friend… I did NOT see this coming.

cards.question: The centurion tells Jesus he is not worthy. Not worthy of what?

answers.text: Having Jesus come under his roof

cards.question: So the centurion asks for something else. He asks Jesus to just say the ___, and his servant will be healed.

cards.text: Then he explains that he's a man under authority, with soldiers under him: he tells one to go, and he goes, and another to come, and he comes. Friend, I tell my oven timer to stop, and it beeps LOUDER.

cards.question: Why does the centurion tell Jesus about the soldiers and the servant under him?

answers.text: He knows a command gets obeyed
He wants Jesus to see his rank
He offers his men to guard Jesus

cards.text: Jesus hears what the centurion said, and He marvels. Then He turns to the people following Him.

cards.question: Jesus turns to the people following Him. What does He say about the centurion's faith?

answers.text: He hasn't found faith this great in Israel
It's as small as a mustard seed for now
It will grow if he keeps on asking

cards.text: Then Jesus says many will come from the east and the west. They'll gather with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, Israel's forefathers, in the kingdom of heaven.

cards.question: Many will come from the east and the west. What will they share with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven?

cards.text: A BANQUET. Friend, you're talking to a stamper in the feast-prep business, and my mustache just stood straight up.

cards.question: Jesus tells the people following Him that many will come from the east and the west to share the banquet in the kingdom of heaven. He says the sons of the kingdom will share in the banquet too.

cards.text: Instead, Jesus says they'll be thrown into the outer darkness, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth. Then He turns back to the centurion.

cards.question: Jesus tells the centurion to go. It will be done for him just as he has ___.
The centurion's servant is healed at that very hour.

cards.text: Jesus never even steps under that roof. Me? I have to be standing RIGHT on the dough, every single time, or nothing happens.
Next, Jesus arrives at the house of Peter, one of His disciples. He sees Peter's mother-in-law sick in bed with a fever.

cards.question: Peter's mother-in-law is sick in bed with a fever. What does Jesus do?

answers.text: He prays over her all night
He sends Peter for the priest

cards.question: The fever leaves Peter's mother-in-law. What does she do next?

answers.text: She gets up and serves Him
She runs to tell the neighbors

cards.text: Fever gone, and she's UP and serving. Friend, after one long day of baking I need three snooze buttons and a pep talk.
When evening comes, many who are demon-possessed are brought to Jesus. The sick are brought too.

cards.question: The centurion said Jesus could just say the word. That evening, Jesus drives out the spirits with a ___.
That evening, Jesus heals some of the sick who are brought to Him, but not all of them.

cards.text: Then the passage steps back and tells us what all of this was for.

cards.question: Jesus heals a leper, a servant, a fever and a whole evening crowd. What does all this fulfill?

answers.text: What Moses wrote in the Law
What King David sang in a psalm

cards.text: Isaiah said it: “He took up our infirmities and carried our diseases.” A leper, a servant, a fever, a crowd at evening, and He carried every one.

findings.problem: This story card has four sentences: 'Then, suddenly, a man with leprosy comes and kneels before Jesus.' 'No appointment, no heads-up, no “you free Tuesday?”' and 'Just SUDDENLY.' Only the opening card may go past 2 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The setup 'Jesus answers the leper with more than words' rules out the wrong answer 'He tells him to wash in the Jordan', because that answer is only words. The baker can drop it without reasoning about the passage.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: 'I waited YEARS for somebody to open my drawer' contradicts the backstory. The drawer opened often, for scissors or tape, and the light came in each time. What he waited for was to be remembered and put back to work. The joke changes a fact of his world instead of making up a small moment around it.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: 'Just say the prayer' and 'just say the blessing' mean nearly the same as 'just say the word': Jesus speaks from a distance and the servant is healed. A baker could argue either is right. All three answers carry the same meaning, so the blank only tests wording the baker hasn't seen.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: This story card is only a joke reacting to the banquet the baker just answered on card 4. It tells no new part of the passage and doesn't move the passage forward.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'asked' is a near-match. 'It will be done for him just as he has asked' is arguably true, since the servant is healed as the centurion asked.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: This story card recaps that the servant was healed without Jesus going under the roof, then adds a joke. It tells no new part of the passage and doesn't move the passage forward.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: 'Fever gone, and she's UP and serving' recaps the answer to card 13, then adds a joke. It tells no new part of the passage and doesn't move the passage forward.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The setup 'The centurion said Jesus could just say the word' points straight at 'word' and rules out 'touch' and 'prayer'. The card goes beyond an easy follow-up: the question hands over its own answer.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: 'What all of this was for' says Matthew 8:17's 'This' covers the whole passage. The text says 'This was to fulfill' right after the evening healings and doesn't say how far 'This' reaches.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The question says the healing of the leper, the servant, the fever and the evening crowd all fulfill Isaiah. Matthew 8:17 says 'This was to fulfill', right after verse 16, and doesn't say how far 'This' reaches. 'Heals … a fever' also reads oddly. Jesus heals Peter's mother-in-law.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: 'A leper, a servant, a fever, a crowd at evening, and He carried every one' recaps the passage. It also says Isaiah's words cover every earlier healing, which Matthew 8:17 doesn't state, and it cites only Matthew 8:17 while using verses 2 to 16.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.
